---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API — send and read messages, list and create channels, find users, search messages, and manage threads, reactions, and file uploads. Use when Gemini CLI needs to perform Slack operations (messaging, channel and user management, search) using a bot or user token.
---

# Slack API

Call the Slack Web API (`https://slack.com/api/`) for messaging, channel and user management, and search, using the bundled helper script and reference.

## Authentication

- Set `SLACK_TOKEN` in the environment to a bot token (`xoxb-...`) or user token (`xoxp-...`). Never pass tokens on the command line.
- Verify the token and learn the caller identity: `node scripts/slack_call.cjs auth.test`
- The calling identity must be a member of any channel it reads or writes. Resolve names to IDs with `conversations.list` and `users.lookupByEmail` (see references/slack-api.md) before messaging.

## Quick start

Every Slack API method is one call:

```bash
SLACK_TOKEN=xoxb-... node scripts/slack_call.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C12345","text":"Hello from Gemini CLI!"}'
```

`scripts/slack_call.cjs`:
- POSTs JSON with `Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN` and prints the JSON response on stdout
- Exits non-zero with a plain-language error when `ok` is `false`
- Retries on HTTP 429 / `rate_limited` using `Retry-After`
- Follows pagination with `--paginate` (merges result arrays, sleeps 1.1s between pages)

## Core workflow

1. **Pick the method** — messaging: `chat.postMessage`; reading: `conversations.history`; listing: `conversations.list` / `users.list`; search: `search.messages`.
2. **Resolve names to IDs** — Slack methods take IDs (`C...` channels, `U...` users, `D...` DMs). Map names → IDs with `conversations.list` / `users.lookupByEmail` first.
3. **Send the request** through `scripts/slack_call.cjs`.
4. **Inspect the result** — check `ok`, honor `response_metadata.next_cursor` (or pass `--paginate`), and back off on `429` / `rate_limited`.

## Formatting messages

- mrkdwn: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `<https://example.com|link text>`, `:tada:`, `<@U123>` mentions, `<#C123>` channel links, `<!channel>` / `<!here>`, and `\n` for line breaks.
- Rich messages: pass a `blocks` array (examples in references/slack-api.md) and keep `mrkdwn: true` on text fields that should render.
- Thread replies: pass the parent message's `thread_ts` to `chat.postMessage`; read threads with `conversations.replies`.

## Reference

Read [references/slack-api.md](references/slack-api.md) when you need:
- Endpoint catalog and parameters (messages, conversations, users, search, reactions, files)
- Pagination and rate-limit behavior
- Error codes and fixes
- Block Kit examples and copy-paste workflows (send a message, read history, create a channel and invite members, DM a user)

## Notes

- Channel names are not stable (renames break name-based lookups); IDs are.
- Timestamps (`ts`) are strings — keep them as strings for `thread_ts` and `latest`/`oldest` (epoch seconds).
- Never log or echo tokens.

# Slack Web API Reference

Use this file when working with Slack API endpoints, pagination, rate limits, formatting, or common workflows. All calls go through `scripts/slack_call.cjs` in the skill root (see SKILL.md).

## Contents

1. [Authentication and scopes](#authentication-and-scopes)
2. [Endpoint catalog](#endpoint-catalog)
3. [Pagination](#pagination)
4. [Rate limits](#rate-limits)
5. [Errors and fixes](#errors-and-fixes)
6. [Message formatting (mrkdwn)](#message-formatting-mrkdwn)
7. [Block Kit](#block-kit)
8. [Threads](#threads)
9. [Common workflows](#common-workflows)

## Authentication and scopes

- Base URL: `https://slack.com/api/`. All methods are `POST` with JSON body and header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Token prefixes: `xoxb-...` bot token, `xoxp-...` user token, `xapp-...` app-level token (Socket Mode/Events API only — not for Web API calls).
- A bot token can only access conversations the bot is a member of. A user token acts as a user (subject to user membership and admin settings).
- The token's identity must have the required scope for each method; otherwise the API returns `missing_scope` with `needed`/`provided` fields.

| Operation | Scopes |
| --- | --- |
| Send / update / delete messages | `chat:write` |
| Read channel history | `channels:history`, `groups:history`, `im:history`, `mpim:history` |
| List channels / DMs | `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read` |
| Create / invite / rename / archive channels | `channels:manage`, `groups:write` |
| List users, user info | `users:read` (+ `users:read.email` for email lookup) |
| Search messages | `search:read` (user token) |
| Add / remove reactions | `reactions:write` |
| Upload files | `files:write` |
| Open DMs | `im:write` |

## Endpoint catalog

### Verify

**`auth.test`** — no arguments. Returns `ok`, `url`, `team`, `user`, `user_id`, `team_id`. Use it first to confirm the token works and to learn the caller's user ID.

### Messages (`chat.*`)

**`chat.postMessage`** — send a message.
- Params: `channel` (ID, required), `text`, `blocks`, `thread_ts`, `reply_broadcast`, `mrkdwn` (default `true`), `link_names`, `unfurl_links`, `unfurl_media`.
- Returns `channel`, `ts`, `message`.
- Plain text is capped at 40,000 chars (`msg_too_long` beyond that).

**`chat.update`** — edit a message. Params: `channel`, `ts`, `text`/`blocks`. Returns `ts` and `message`.

**`chat.delete`** — delete a message. Params: `channel`, `ts`.

**`chat.postEphemeral`** — send a message visible only to one user. Params: `channel`, `user`, `text`. Returns `message_ts`.

### Conversations (`conversations.*`)

**`conversations.list`** — list channels/DMs the token can see.
- Params: `types` (comma-separated: `public_channel` (default), `private_channel`, `mpim`, `im`), `limit`, `cursor`, `exclude_archived` (default `true`).
- Returns `channels` (each with `id`, `name`, `is_private`, `is_member`, `is_archived`, `members` when requested via `conversations.members`).
- Use this to resolve channel names → IDs.

**`conversations.history`** — read messages in a channel. Params: `channel` (required), `limit` (default 100), `cursor`, `inclusive`, `latest`, `oldest` (epoch seconds; default newest→oldest). Returns `messages` (newest first), `has_more`, `response_metadata.next_cursor`.

**`conversations.replies`** — read a thread. Params: `channel`, `ts` (parent message timestamp). Returns `messages` (parent first, then replies), `has_more`.

**`conversations.create`** — create a channel. Params: `name`, `is_private` (default `false`; cannot be changed later). Returns `channel`.

**`conversations.invite`** — invite users to a channel. Params: `channel`, `users` (comma-separated user IDs). The caller must already be a member.

**`conversations.rename`** — rename a channel. Params: `channel`, `name`.

**`conversations.archive`** / **`conversations.unarchive`** — archive/restore. Params: `channel`.

**`conversations.open`** — get or create a DM with a user. Params: `user`. Returns `channel` (use `channel.id` as the `channel` for `chat.postMessage`).

**`conversations.members`** — list member user IDs of a channel. Params: `channel`, `limit`, `cursor`. Returns `members`.

**`conversations.info`** — channel metadata. Params: `channel`, `include_num_members`.

### Users (`users.*`)

**`users.list`** — list workspace users. Params: `limit`, `cursor`. Returns `members` (each with `id`, `name`, `real_name`, `profile.email`, `is_bot`, `deleted`). Can be large and slow on big workspaces — prefer targeted lookups.

**`users.info`** — user details. Params: `user`. Returns `user`.

**`users.lookupByEmail`** — find a user by email. Params: `email`. Returns `user`. Requires `users:read.email`.

### Search

**`search.messages`** — search messages. Params: `query` (required), `count` (default 20, max 100), `cursor`, `sort` (`score` | `timestamp`), `sort_dir` (`asc` | `desc`), `highlight`. Returns `messages.matches` (each with `channel`, `ts`, `text`, `user`, `permalink`). Note: search indexing can lag a few seconds behind new messages.

### Reactions

**`reactions.add`** — add a reaction. Params: `channel`, `name` (emoji without colons, e.g. `white_check_mark`), `timestamp` (message `ts`). Related: `reactions.remove`, `reactions.get`.

### Files

**`files.upload`** — legacy upload (deprecated; still works for now). Params: `channels` (comma-separated IDs), `content` (string), `filename`, `title`, `thread_ts`. Works through the helper script.

**Current upload flow** (preferred):
1. `files.getUploadURLExternal` with `filename`, `length` (byte length), `alt_txt` → returns `upload_url`, `file_id`.
2. Upload the raw file bytes to `upload_url` with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` (binary body — the helper script cannot do this step; use `curl -F file=@...` or a short Node `fetch` script).
3. `files.completeUploadExternal` with `files: [{"id": "<file_id>", "title": "..."}]`, `channel_id`, `thread_ts`.

## Pagination

- List/history/search methods return `response_metadata.next_cursor` when more results exist.
- Pass that value as `cursor` in the next call; repeat until `next_cursor` is empty.
- The helper script does this automatically with `--paginate` (merges top-level arrays; stops after `--limit N` pages, default 20).
- Prefer cursor pagination over large `limit` values — Slack caps page size per method.

## Rate limits

- Slack enforces per-method tiered rate limits per workspace. HTTP 429 responses include a `Retry-After` header (seconds) — wait that long before retrying.
- Legacy style: `{"ok": false, "error": "rate_limited", "retry_after": N}`.
- Bots sending messages are limited to roughly 1 message/second per channel (20/second overall); batch sends need small delays between calls.
- Strategy: honor `Retry-After`, add exponential backoff with jitter, and cap retries (the helper retries 3 times).

## Errors and fixes

Responses have `ok: false` plus an `error` string. Common values:

| Error | Meaning / fix |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_auth` | Token is bad or revoked — check `SLACK_TOKEN`. |
| `missing_scope` | Token lacks a required scope (`needed` field names it) — add the scope to the app and reinstall. |
| `not_in_channel` | Caller is not a member — join/invite the bot first (`conversations.join` or `conversations.invite`). |
| `channel_not_found` | Wrong or archived ID — re-resolve via `conversations.list`. |
| `is_archived` | Channel archived — unarchive before posting. |
| `name_taken` | Channel name exists — pick another name. |
| `user_not_found` | Wrong user ID — resolve via `users.lookupByEmail`. |
| `already_in_channel` | User is already a member — no action needed. |
| `user_not_in_channel` | User must join before being mentioned/added. |
| `restricted_action` | Enterprise/guest policy blocks the action. |
| `msg_too_long` | Text exceeds 40,000 chars — shorten. |
| `invalid_blocks` | Block Kit JSON malformed — validate structure. |
| `rate_limited` | Slow down and retry after `retry_after`. |

## Message formatting (mrkdwn)

- `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~`, `` `code` ``, triple-backtick for preformatted blocks.
- Links: `<https://example.com|display text>`; escape literal `<`, `>`, `&` as `<`, `>`, `&`.
- Mentions: `<@U123>`, channel links `<#C123>`, special mentions `<!channel>`, `<!here>`, `<!everyone>`.
- Date formatting: `<!date^1392734382^{date_long}|fallback text>`.
- Emoji: `:tada:`. Line breaks: `\n`. Message text supports these natively; block text needs `mrkdwn: true` on the text object.

## Block Kit

Pass a `blocks` array to `chat.postMessage` for rich layouts. Keep it to essential types:

```json
{
  "channel": "C12345",
  "blocks": [
    { "type": "header", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Daily summary" } },
    { "type": "section", "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*3 new messages* in #general" } },
    { "type": "context", "elements": [ { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Generated by Gemini CLI" } ] },
    { "type": "divider" }
  ]
}
```

Notes: `header` takes `plain_text` only; `section`/`context` text can be `mrkdwn`. Interactive elements (`actions` with buttons) only work when the app has interactivity enabled — otherwise they render but do nothing, so prefer plain sections for read-only bots.

## Threads

1. Post the parent message with `chat.postMessage` → returns `ts`.
2. Reply by calling `chat.postMessage` again with the same `channel` and `thread_ts: "<parent ts>"`.
3. Pass `reply_broadcast: true` to also post the reply to the channel.
4. Read the whole thread with `conversations.replies` (`channel`, `ts` = parent ts).

## Common workflows

**Send a message to a channel by name**
```bash
node scripts/slack_call.cjs conversations.list '{"types":"public_channel","limit":200}' --paginate
# find the id for the channel name, then:
node scripts/slack_call.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C12345","text":"Hello!"}'
```

**Read the last 10 messages in a channel**
```bash
node scripts/slack_call.cjs conversations.history '{"channel":"C12345","limit":10}'
```

**Create a channel and invite people**
```bash
node scripts/slack_call.cjs conversations.create '{"name":"project-orbital"}'
node scripts/slack_call.cjs users.lookupByEmail '{"email":"ada@example.com"}'
node scripts/slack_call.cjs conversations.invite '{"channel":"C12345","users":"U111,U222"}'
```

**DM a user**
```bash
node scripts/slack_call.cjs users.lookupByEmail '{"email":"ada@example.com"}'
node scripts/slack_call.cjs conversations.open '{"user":"U111"}'
node scripts/slack_call.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"D222","text":"Hi Ada!"}'
```

**Search recent messages**
```bash
node scripts/slack_call.cjs search.messages '{"query":"deploy failed","sort":"timestamp","sort_dir":"desc","count":20}'
```

description: Interact with the Slack Web API to send, update, and delete messages; list and join channels and conversations; read message history; manage reactions, files, and emoji; look up users; search the workspace; and handle pagination, rate limits, and errors. Use when the user asks to post to Slack, build Slack notifications or bots, query Slack conversations or users, or perform any Slack API integration using an OAuth token.
---

# Slack API Interaction

Use the Slack Web API over HTTPS. Every request goes to `https://slack.com/api/<method>` with the bot or user OAuth token in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.

## Authentication

- Obtain the token from the user, the `SLACK_TOKEN` env var, or a `.env` file.
- Bot tokens start with `xoxb-`; user tokens start with `xoxp-`.
- The token must have the scopes required by the method (see https://api.slack.com/scopes).
- Common bot scopes: `chat:write`, `channels:read`, `channels:history`, `groups:read`, `groups:history`, `im:read`, `im:history`, `users:read`, `reactions:write`, `files:write`, `emoji:read`, `team:read`.
- Validate any unknown token with `auth.test` before building on it.

## Response envelope

Every response is JSON:

```json
{ "ok": true, ...method-specific fields }
{ "ok": false, "error": "channel_not_found", "response_metadata": { "messages": [...] } }
```

- Always check `ok`. On failure, report `error` and any `response_metadata.messages`.
- Send JSON bodies with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`.

## Core workflow

1. Identify the token and confirm the needed scopes.
2. Pick the method (see table) and build the payload.
3. Send the request with `curl` or the helper script below.
4. Verify `ok: true`; otherwise surface the error and fix the payload.
5. Paginate when the response contains `response_metadata.next_cursor`.
6. On HTTP 429, honor `Retry-After` and back off.

## Common methods

| Method | Purpose | Key parameters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| chat.postMessage | Send a message to a channel, DM, or thread | channel, text, blocks, thread_ts, mrkdwn, link_names |
| chat.postEphemeral | Send a message visible only to one user | channel, user, text |
| chat.update | Edit a message | channel, ts, text, blocks |
| chat.delete | Delete a message | channel, ts |
| chat.scheduleMessage | Schedule a message | channel, text, post_at |
| conversations.list | List channels, groups, DMs, MPIMs | types, cursor, limit |
| conversations.history | Read recent messages in a conversation | channel, cursor, limit, oldest, latest |
| conversations.info | Get conversation metadata | channel |
| conversations.join | Join a public channel | channel |
| conversations.leave | Leave a conversation | channel |
| users.list / users.info | List / get workspace users | cursor / user |
| users.lookupByEmail | Find a user by email | email |
| users.getPresence | Check user presence | user |
| reactions.add / remove | Add / remove an emoji reaction | channel, name, timestamp |
| files.getUploadURLExternal + files.completeUploadExternal | Upload files | filename, length, channels, file_id, files |
| emoji.list | List custom emoji | — |
| search.messages | Search messages | query, cursor |
| team.info | Workspace info | — |
| auth.test | Validate token and get bot/user id | — |

Note: `conversations.*` covers public channels, private channels (groups), DMs (im), and multi-person DMs (mpim). Filter with `types=public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim`.

## Message formatting

- Use mrkdwn for light formatting: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `>quote`, `~strike~`.
- Use the Blocks API (`blocks`) for rich messages: `section`, `divider`, `actions`, `context`, `image`, `input`, `header`.
- `link_names: true` turns @mentions and #channels into links.
- For threaded replies, pass the parent message's `ts` as `thread_ts`; optionally add `reply_broadcast: true`.
- Legacy `attachments` still work but prefer `blocks`.

## Pagination

Cursor-based pagination:

1. Send the request with `limit` (max 200 for most list methods) and optional `cursor`.
2. Read `response_metadata.next_cursor` from the response.
3. If non-empty, repeat with `cursor=<next_cursor>`; otherwise stop.
4. Guard loops with a maximum iteration count (e.g., 1000) to avoid runaway requests.

## Rate limits and retries

- Slack rate-limits per method per workspace in tiers (Tier 1 ≈ 1+ req/s, Tier 4 ≈ 100 req/min).
- On HTTP 429, read the `Retry-After` header and wait that many seconds before retrying.
- Retry transient network failures with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, ...).

## Common errors

- `not_authed` / `invalid_auth` — bad or missing token; verify the token and scopes.
- `account_inactive` / `token_revoked` — token is invalid; ask the user for a fresh token.
- `missing_scope` — the token lacks the required scope; reinstall the app with the scope.
- `channel_not_found` — the channel does not exist or the bot is not a member; join it first or verify the ID/name.
- `is_archived` — the channel is archived; use a different channel.
- `invalid_blocks` / `invalid_arguments` — malformed payload; validate the `blocks` JSON.
- `ratelimited` — slow down; honor `Retry-After`.
- `name_taken` — the username/emoji already exists.

## Helper script

For deterministic calls, write the following to `scripts/slack_call.cjs` and run it with Node 18+:

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Usage: node slack_call.cjs <method> ['<json-payload>'] [token]
// Example: node slack_call.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"#general","text":"Hello"}' "$SLACK_TOKEN"
(async () => {
  const method = process.argv[2];
  const payload = JSON.parse(process.argv[3] || '{}');
  const token = process.argv[4] || process.env.SLACK_TOKEN;
  if (!method || !token) {
    console.error('Usage: node slack_call.cjs <method> [json-payload] [token]');
    process.exit(2);
  }
  const res = await fetch('https://slack.com/api/' + method, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + token,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(payload),
  });
  const body = await res.json();
  if (body.ok) {
    console.log('OK ' + method + ': ' + JSON.stringify(body).slice(0, 2000));
  } else {
    console.error('ERROR ' + method + ': ' + body.error +
      (body.response_metadata && body.response_metadata.messages
        ? ' — ' + body.response_metadata.messages.join('; ') : ''));
    process.exitCode = 1;
  }
})();
```

The script prints a short JSON summary on success and a clear error message on failure. Keep stdout LLM-friendly: truncate long payloads and paginate large listings.

## Reference docs

- Full method reference: https://api.slack.com/methods
- Scopes: https://api.slack.com/scopes
- Rate limits: https://api.slack.com/docs/rate-limits
- Blocks kit: https://api.slack.com/block-kit
- OAuth (installing apps): https://api.slack.com/authentication/oauth

1. **Pick the method** — messaging: `chat.postMessage`; reading: `conversations.history`; listing: `conversations.list` / `users.list`; search: `search.messages`.
2. **Resolve names to IDs** — Slack methods take IDs (`C...` channels, `U...` users, `D...` DMs). Map names → IDs with `conversations.list` / `users.lookupByEmail` first.
3. **Send the request** through `scripts/slack_call.cjs`.
4. **Inspect the result** — check `ok`, honor `response_metadata.next_cursor` (or pass `--paginate`), and back off on `429` / `rate_limited`.

## Formatting messages

- mrkdwn: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `<https://example.com|link text>`, `:tada:`, `<@U123>` mentions, `<#C123>` channel links, `<!channel>` / `<!here>`, and `\n` for line breaks.
- Rich messages: pass a `blocks` array (examples in references/slack-api.md) and keep `mrkdwn: true` on text fields that should render.
- Thread replies: pass the parent message's `thread_ts` to `chat.postMessage`; read threads with `conversations.replies`.

## Reference

Read [references/slack-api.md](references/slack-api.md) when you need:
- Endpoint catalog and parameters (messages, conversations, users, search, reactions, files)
- Pagination and rate-limit behavior
- Error codes and fixes
- Block Kit examples and copy-paste workflows (send a message, read history, create a channel and invite members, DM a user)

## Notes

- Channel names are not stable (renames break name-based lookups); IDs are.
- Timestamps (`ts`) are strings — keep them as strings for `thread_ts` and `latest`/`oldest` (epoch seconds).
- Never log or echo tokens.

## Authentication and scopes

- Base URL: `https://slack.com/api/`. All methods are `POST` with JSON body and header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Token prefixes: `xoxb-...` bot token, `xoxp-...` user token, `xapp-...` app-level token (Socket Mode/Events API only — not for Web API calls).
- A bot token can only access conversations the bot is a member of. A user token acts as a user (subject to user membership and admin settings).
- The token's identity must have the required scope for each method; otherwise the API returns `missing_scope` with `needed`/`provided` fields.

| Operation | Scopes |
| --- | --- |
| Send / update / delete messages | `chat:write` |
| Read channel history | `channels:history`, `groups:history`, `im:history`, `mpim:history` |
| List channels / DMs | `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read` |
| Create / invite / rename / archive channels | `channels:manage`, `groups:write` |
| List users, user info | `users:read` (+ `users:read.email` for email lookup) |
| Search messages | `search:read` (user token) |
| Add / remove reactions | `reactions:write` |
| Upload files | `files:write` |
| Open DMs | `im:write` |

## Endpoint catalog

### Verify

**`auth.test`** — no arguments. Returns `ok`, `url`, `team`, `user`, `user_id`, `team_id`. Use it first to confirm the token works and to learn the caller's user ID.

### Messages (`chat.*`)

**`chat.postMessage`** — send a message.
- Params: `channel` (ID, required), `text`, `blocks`, `thread_ts`, `reply_broadcast`, `mrkdwn` (default `true`), `link_names`, `unfurl_links`, `unfurl_media`.
- Returns `channel`, `ts`, `message`.
- Plain text is capped at 40,000 chars (`msg_too_long` beyond that).

**`chat.update`** — edit a message. Params: `channel`, `ts`, `text`/`blocks`. Returns `ts` and `message`.

**`chat.delete`** — delete a message. Params: `channel`, `ts`.

**`chat.postEphemeral`** — send a message visible only to one user. Params: `channel`, `user`, `text`. Returns `message_ts`.

### Conversations (`conversations.*`)

**`conversations.list`** — list channels/DMs the token can see.
- Params: `types` (comma-separated: `public_channel` (default), `private_channel`, `mpim`, `im`), `limit`, `cursor`, `exclude_archived` (default `true`).
- Returns `channels` (each with `id`, `name`, `is_private`, `is_member`, `is_archived`, `members` when requested via `conversations.members`).
- Use this to resolve channel names → IDs.

**`conversations.history`** — read messages in a channel. Params: `channel` (required), `limit` (default 100), `cursor`, `inclusive`, `latest`, `oldest` (epoch seconds; default newest→oldest). Returns `messages` (newest first), `has_more`, `response_metadata.next_cursor`.

**`conversations.replies`** — read a thread. Params: `channel`, `ts` (parent message timestamp). Returns `messages` (parent first, then replies), `has_more`.

**`conversations.create`** — create a channel. Params: `name`, `is_private` (default `false`; cannot be changed later). Returns `channel`.

**`conversations.invite`** — invite users to a channel. Params: `channel`, `users` (comma-separated user IDs). The caller must already be a member.

**`conversations.rename`** — rename a channel. Params: `channel`, `name`.

**`conversations.archive`** / **`conversations.unarchive`** — archive/restore. Params: `channel`.

**`conversations.open`** — get or create a DM with a user. Params: `user`. Returns `channel` (use `channel.id` as the `channel` for `chat.postMessage`).

**`conversations.members`** — list member user IDs of a channel. Params: `channel`, `limit`, `cursor`. Returns `members`.

**`conversations.info`** — channel metadata. Params: `channel`, `include_num_members`.

### Users (`users.*`)

**`users.list`** — list workspace users. Params: `limit`, `cursor`. Returns `members` (each with `id`, `name`, `real_name`, `profile.email`, `is_bot`, `deleted`). Can be large and slow on big workspaces — prefer targeted lookups.

**`users.info`** — user details. Params: `user`. Returns `user`.

**`users.lookupByEmail`** — find a user by email. Params: `email`. Returns `user`. Requires `users:read.email`.

### Search

**`search.messages`** — search messages. Params: `query` (required), `count` (default 20, max 100), `cursor`, `sort` (`score` | `timestamp`), `sort_dir` (`asc` | `desc`), `highlight`. Returns `messages.matches` (each with `channel`, `ts`, `text`, `user`, `permalink`). Note: search indexing can lag a few seconds behind new messages.

### Reactions

**`reactions.add`** — add a reaction. Params: `channel`, `name` (emoji without colons, e.g. `white_check_mark`), `timestamp` (message `ts`). Related: `reactions.remove`, `reactions.get`.

### Files

**`files.upload`** — legacy upload (deprecated; still works for now). Params: `channels` (comma-separated IDs), `content` (string), `filename`, `title`, `thread_ts`. Works through the helper script.

**Current upload flow** (preferred):
1. `files.getUploadURLExternal` with `filename`, `length` (byte length), `alt_txt` → returns `upload_url`, `file_id`.
2. Upload the raw file bytes to `upload_url` with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` (binary body — the helper script cannot do this step; use `curl -F file=@...` or a short Node `fetch` script).
3. `files.completeUploadExternal` with `files: [{"id": "<file_id>", "title": "..."}]`, `channel_id`, `thread_ts`.

## Pagination

- List/history/search methods return `response_metadata.next_cursor` when more results exist.
- Pass that value as `cursor` in the next call; repeat until `next_cursor` is empty.
- The helper script does this automatically with `--paginate` (merges top-level arrays; stops after `--limit N` pages, default 20).
- Prefer cursor pagination over large `limit` values — Slack caps page size per method.

## Rate limits

- Slack enforces per-method tiered rate limits per workspace. HTTP 429 responses include a `Retry-After` header (seconds) — wait that long before retrying.
- Legacy style: `{"ok": false, "error": "rate_limited", "retry_after": N}`.
- Bots sending messages are limited to roughly 1 message/second per channel (20/second overall); batch sends need small delays between calls.
- Strategy: honor `Retry-After`, add exponential backoff with jitter, and cap retries (the helper retries 3 times).

## Errors and fixes

Responses have `ok: false` plus an `error` string. Common values:

| Error | Meaning / fix |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_auth` | Token is bad or revoked — check `SLACK_TOKEN`. |
| `missing_scope` | Token lacks a required scope (`needed` field names it) — add the scope to the app and reinstall. |
| `not_in_channel` | Caller is not a member — join/invite the bot first (`conversations.join` or `conversations.invite`). |
| `channel_not_found` | Wrong or archived ID — re-resolve via `conversations.list`. |
| `is_archived` | Channel archived — unarchive before posting. |
| `name_taken` | Channel name exists — pick another name. |
| `user_not_found` | Wrong user ID — resolve via `users.lookupByEmail`. |
| `already_in_channel` | User is already a member — no action needed. |
| `user_not_in_channel` | User must join before being mentioned/added. |
| `restricted_action` | Enterprise/guest policy blocks the action. |
| `msg_too_long` | Text exceeds 40,000 chars — shorten. |
| `invalid_blocks` | Block Kit JSON malformed — validate structure. |
| `rate_limited` | Slow down and retry after `retry_after`. |

## Message formatting (mrkdwn)

- `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~`, `` `code` ``, triple-backtick for preformatted blocks.
- Links: `<https://example.com|display text>`; escape literal `<`, `>`, `&` as `<`, `>`, `&`.
- Mentions: `<@U123>`, channel links `<#C123>`, special mentions `<!channel>`, `<!here>`, `<!everyone>`.
- Date formatting: `<!date^1392734382^{date_long}|fallback text>`.
- Emoji: `:tada:`. Line breaks: `\n`. Message text supports these natively; block text needs `mrkdwn: true` on the text object.

## Block Kit

Pass a `blocks` array to `chat.postMessage` for rich layouts. Keep it to essential types:

```json
{
  "channel": "C12345",
  "blocks": [
    { "type": "header", "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Daily summary" } },
    { "type": "section", "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*3 new messages* in #general" } },
    { "type": "context", "elements": [ { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Generated by Gemini CLI" } ] },
    { "type": "divider" }
  ]
}
```

Notes: `header` takes `plain_text` only; `section`/`context` text can be `mrkdwn`. Interactive elements (`actions` with buttons) only work when the app has interactivity enabled — otherwise they render but do nothing, so prefer plain sections for read-only bots.

## Threads

1. Post the parent message with `chat.postMessage` → returns `ts`.
2. Reply by calling `chat.postMessage` again with the same `channel` and `thread_ts: "<parent ts>"`.
3. Pass `reply_broadcast: true` to also post the reply to the channel.
4. Read the whole thread with `conversations.replies` (`channel`, `ts` = parent ts).

## Common workflows

**Send a message to a channel by name**
```bash
node scripts/slack_call.cjs conversations.list '{"types":"public_channel","limit":200}' --paginate
# find the id for the channel name, then:
node scripts/slack_call.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C12345","text":"Hello!"}'
```

**Read the last 10 messages in a channel**
```bash
node scripts/slack_call.cjs conversations.history '{"channel":"C12345","limit":10}'
```

**Create a channel and invite people**
```bash
node scripts/slack_call.cjs conversations.create '{"name":"project-orbital"}'
node scripts/slack_call.cjs users.lookupByEmail '{"email":"ada@example.com"}'
node scripts/slack_call.cjs conversations.invite '{"channel":"C12345","users":"U111,U222"}'
```

**DM a user**
```bash
node scripts/slack_call.cjs users.lookupByEmail '{"email":"ada@example.com"}'
node scripts/slack_call.cjs conversations.open '{"user":"U111"}'
node scripts/slack_call.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"D222","text":"Hi Ada!"}'
```

**Search recent messages**
```bash
node scripts/slack_call.cjs search.messages '{"query":"deploy failed","sort":"timestamp","sort_dir":"desc","count":20}'
```

# Slack API Interaction

Use the Slack Web API over HTTPS. Every request goes to `https://slack.com/api/<method>` with the bot or user OAuth token in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.

## Authentication

- Obtain the token from the user, the `SLACK_TOKEN` env var, or a `.env` file.
- Bot tokens start with `xoxb-`; user tokens start with `xoxp-`.
- The token must have the scopes required by the method (see https://api.slack.com/scopes).
- Common bot scopes: `chat:write`, `channels:read`, `channels:history`, `groups:read`, `groups:history`, `im:read`, `im:history`, `users:read`, `reactions:write`, `files:write`, `emoji:read`, `team:read`.
- Validate any unknown token with `auth.test` before building on it.

## Response envelope

Every response is JSON:

```json
{ "ok": true, ...method-specific fields }
{ "ok": false, "error": "channel_not_found", "response_metadata": { "messages": [...] } }
```

- Always check `ok`. On failure, report `error` and any `response_metadata.messages`.
- Send JSON bodies with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`.

## Core workflow

1. Identify the token and confirm the needed scopes.
2. Pick the method (see table) and build the payload.
3. Send the request with `curl` or the helper script below.
4. Verify `ok: true`; otherwise surface the error and fix the payload.
5. Paginate when the response contains `response_metadata.next_cursor`.
6. On HTTP 429, honor `Retry-After` and back off.

## Common methods

| Method | Purpose | Key parameters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| chat.postMessage | Send a message to a channel, DM, or thread | channel, text, blocks, thread_ts, mrkdwn, link_names |
| chat.postEphemeral | Send a message visible only to one user | channel, user, text |
| chat.update | Edit a message | channel, ts, text, blocks |
| chat.delete | Delete a message | channel, ts |
| chat.scheduleMessage | Schedule a message | channel, text, post_at |
| conversations.list | List channels, groups, DMs, MPIMs | types, cursor, limit |
| conversations.history | Read recent messages in a conversation | channel, cursor, limit, oldest, latest |
| conversations.info | Get conversation metadata | channel |
| conversations.join | Join a public channel | channel |
| conversations.leave | Leave a conversation | channel |
| users.list / users.info | List / get workspace users | cursor / user |
| users.lookupByEmail | Find a user by email | email |
| users.getPresence | Check user presence | user |
| reactions.add / remove | Add / remove an emoji reaction | channel, name, timestamp |
| files.getUploadURLExternal + files.completeUploadExternal | Upload files | filename, length, channels, file_id, files |
| emoji.list | List custom emoji | — |
| search.messages | Search messages | query, cursor |
| team.info | Workspace info | — |
| auth.test | Validate token and get bot/user id | — |

Note: `conversations.*` covers public channels, private channels (groups), DMs (im), and multi-person DMs (mpim). Filter with `types=public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim`.

## Message formatting

- Use mrkdwn for light formatting: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `>quote`, `~strike~`.
- Use the Blocks API (`blocks`) for rich messages: `section`, `divider`, `actions`, `context`, `image`, `input`, `header`.
- `link_names: true` turns @mentions and #channels into links.
- For threaded replies, pass the parent message's `ts` as `thread_ts`; optionally add `reply_broadcast: true`.
- Legacy `attachments` still work but prefer `blocks`.

## Pagination

Cursor-based pagination:

1. Send the request with `limit` (max 200 for most list methods) and optional `cursor`.
2. Read `response_metadata.next_cursor` from the response.
3. If non-empty, repeat with `cursor=<next_cursor>`; otherwise stop.
4. Guard loops with a maximum iteration count (e.g., 1000) to avoid runaway requests.

## Rate limits and retries

- Slack rate-limits per method per workspace in tiers (Tier 1 ≈ 1+ req/s, Tier 4 ≈ 100 req/min).
- On HTTP 429, read the `Retry-After` header and wait that many seconds before retrying.
- Retry transient network failures with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, ...).

## Common errors

- `not_authed` / `invalid_auth` — bad or missing token; verify the token and scopes.
- `account_inactive` / `token_revoked` — token is invalid; ask the user for a fresh token.
- `missing_scope` — the token lacks the required scope; reinstall the app with the scope.
- `channel_not_found` — the channel does not exist or the bot is not a member; join it first or verify the ID/name.
- `is_archived` — the channel is archived; use a different channel.
- `invalid_blocks` / `invalid_arguments` — malformed payload; validate the `blocks` JSON.
- `ratelimited` — slow down; honor `Retry-After`.
- `name_taken` — the username/emoji already exists.

## Helper script

For deterministic calls, write the following to `scripts/slack_call.cjs` and run it with Node 18+:

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Usage: node slack_call.cjs <method> ['<json-payload>'] [token]
// Example: node slack_call.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"#general","text":"Hello"}' "$SLACK_TOKEN"
(async () => {
  const method = process.argv[2];
  const payload = JSON.parse(process.argv[3] || '{}');
  const token = process.argv[4] || process.env.SLACK_TOKEN;
  if (!method || !token) {
    console.error('Usage: node slack_call.cjs <method> [json-payload] [token]');
    process.exit(2);
  }
  const res = await fetch('https://slack.com/api/' + method, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + token,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(payload),
  });
  const body = await res.json();
  if (body.ok) {
    console.log('OK ' + method + ': ' + JSON.stringify(body).slice(0, 2000));
  } else {
    console.error('ERROR ' + method + ': ' + body.error +
      (body.response_metadata && body.response_metadata.messages
        ? ' — ' + body.response_metadata.messages.join('; ') : ''));
    process.exitCode = 1;
  }
})();
```

The script prints a short JSON summary on success and a clear error message on failure. Keep stdout LLM-friendly: truncate long payloads and paginate large listings.
